title: "Networks: do semantic and phonological network structure predict word learning in ASD?"
author: "ASD CDI team"
date: '2026-11-05'
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
params:
  exclude_dx_unconfirmed: false  # sensitivity: drop collections without confirmed ASD dx (2024, 9)
  tier_A_only: false             # sensitivity: only collections with trust tier A
  include_flagged: false         # include collections that fail the item-profile check (WS 2024)
---

```{r setup, message=F, warning=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(feather)
source("helper_functions/network_growth.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = F, warning = F)
theme_set(theme_classic())
```

This notebook replaces the earlier version, which depended on rwebppl, espeak and pre-QC feather caches.
It is now built on the cleaned ASD data from `01_prep_data.Rmd`.

- **Word set.** We use the 312 CDI:WS nouns with semantic and phonological network data.
  The networks are defined over these words, so TD and ASD share the same networks.
  The groups differ only in when they learn each word.
- **Semantic network.** Two nouns are linked if either is a free-association response to the other (`in_files/association_cue_target.csv`).
- **Phonological network.** Two nouns are linked if their IPA transcriptions are within edit distance 2.
  The IPA comes from the earlier espeak run, cached in `saved_data/data_static_pred_TD.feather`.
  It depends only on the word, not on the children.
- **Frequency and length** come from the same file.

```{r load}
load("data/nda_private/cached_data.Rds")       # from 01_prep_data.Rmd (gitignored, NDA)
base::load("data/eng_ws_raw_data.Rds")          # Wordbank English (American) WS

words <- read_feather("saved_data/data_static_pred_TD.feather") %>%
  filter(measure == "produces") %>%
  distinct(definition, uni_lemma, IPA, length, frequency) %>%
  arrange(definition)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(words$definition))

asd_ws <- d_asd_ws
if (params$exclude_dx_unconfirmed) asd_ws <- asd_ws %>% filter(!asd_dx_unconfirmed)
if (params$tier_A_only) asd_ws <- asd_ws %>% filter(tier == "A")
if (!params$include_flagged) asd_ws <- asd_ws %>% filter(item_profile_ok)

td_long <- eng_ws %>% filter(definition %in% words$definition) %>%
  transmute(id = data_id, definition, age, produces = as.integer(produces))
asd_long <- asd_ws %>% filter(definition %in% words$definition) %>%
  transmute(id = row, definition, age, produces = as.integer(value))
```

`r if (params$exclude_dx_unconfirmed) "**Sensitivity analysis: collections without confirmed ASD diagnosis excluded.**"`
`r if (params$tier_A_only) "**Sensitivity analysis: tier-A collections only.**"`
`r if (params$include_flagged) "**Sensitivity analysis: includes collections that fail the item-profile check.**" else "Collections that fail the item-profile check in 01_prep_data (WS 2024) are excluded."`

The TD sample has `r n_distinct(td_long$id)` Wordbank administrations, ages `r paste(range(td_long$age), collapse = "–")` months.
The ASD sample has `r n_distinct(asd_long$id)` administrations from `r n_distinct(asd_ws$GUID)` children, ages `r paste(range(asd_long$age), collapse = "–")` months.
For AoA estimation, all of a child's administrations are used: repeated measures affect the uncertainty of the logistic fit, not its point estimate.

# Age of acquisition

The AoA of a word is the age at which a logistic regression of P(produces) on age crosses 50%.

```{r aoa}
aoa <- bind_rows(estimate_aoa(td_long) %>% mutate(group = "TD"),
                 estimate_aoa(asd_long) %>% mutate(group = "ASD")) %>%
  left_join(words, by = "definition")

aoa_wide <- aoa %>% select(definition, group, aoa) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = aoa)
aoa %>% group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(words = n(), min = min(aoa), median = median(aoa), max = max(aoa),
            negative_slope = sum(slope <= 0)) %>% kable(digits = 1)
```

TD and ASD noun AoAs correlate at r = `r round(cor(aoa_wide$TD, aoa_wide$ASD), 2)` (Spearman ρ = `r round(cor(aoa_wide$TD, aoa_wide$ASD, method = "spearman"), 2)`).
The order in which nouns are learned is largely shared, even though children with ASD learn them later.

```{r aoa-scatter, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
ggplot(aoa_wide, aes(TD, ASD)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "grey30") +
  geom_point(alpha = .4) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = aoa_wide %>%
                             mutate(res = resid(lm(ASD ~ TD))) %>%
                             slice_max(abs(res), n = 14),
                           aes(label = definition), size = 3, max.overlaps = 30) +
  labs(x = "TD AoA (months)", y = "ASD AoA (months)")
```

Labelled points are the nouns that children with ASD learn much earlier or later than the TD ordering predicts.

# Networks and static predictors

```{r networks}
cue_target <- read.csv("in_files/association_cue_target.csv", as.is = T)
nets <- list(sem = assoc_adjacency(words$definition, words$uni_lemma, cue_target),
             phono = phono_adjacency(words$definition, words$IPA, threshold = 2))

words <- words %>% mutate(sem_deg = rowSums(nets$sem)[definition],
                          phono_deg = rowSums(nets$phono)[definition])

tibble(network = names(nets),
       edges = map_dbl(nets, ~ sum(.x) / 2),
       mean_degree = map_dbl(nets, ~ mean(rowSums(.x))),
       isolates = map_dbl(nets, ~ sum(rowSums(.x) == 0))) %>% kable(digits = 2)
```

We regress AoA on semantic degree, phonological degree, log frequency and length.
The predictors are z-scored, with missing frequency and length imputed at the mean.
AoA is z-scored within each group, so the coefficients compare the *relative* contribution of each predictor even though ASD AoAs are later and more spread out.

```{r static}
zs <- function(x) as.numeric(scale(replace_na(x, mean(x, na.rm = T))))
static <- aoa %>%
  select(group, definition, aoa) %>%
  left_join(words %>% mutate(across(c(sem_deg, phono_deg, frequency, length), zs)),
            by = "definition") %>%
  group_by(group) %>% mutate(aoa_z = zs(aoa)) %>% ungroup()

preds <- c("sem_deg", "phono_deg", "frequency", "length")
static_coefs <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(preds, function(p) static %>% group_by(group) %>%
            group_modify(~ broom::tidy(lm(reformulate(p, "aoa_z"), data = .x), conf.int = T)) %>%
            mutate(model = "Individual")),
  static %>% group_by(group) %>%
    group_modify(~ broom::tidy(lm(reformulate(preds, "aoa_z"), data = .x), conf.int = T)) %>%
    mutate(model = "Combined")) %>%
  ungroup() %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)")

ggplot(static_coefs, aes(x = estimate, y = term, color = group, shape = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = .6)) +
  labs(x = "Effect on AoA (SD of AoA per SD of predictor)", y = NULL)
```

Do the groups differ? We fit a model on both groups with predictor × group interactions (TD = reference):

```{r static-interaction}
lm(aoa_z ~ (sem_deg + phono_deg + frequency + length) * group,
   data = static %>% mutate(group = factor(group, c("TD", "ASD")))) %>%
  broom::tidy(conf.int = T) %>% filter(str_detect(term, ":")) %>%
  kable(digits = 3)
```

# Network growth models

These models test *how* the lexicon grows.
Each month, the words learned that month are treated as draws from a softmax over all not-yet-learned words.
Each word's utility is α × predictor:

- **PAC** (preferential acquisition) uses a word's degree in the full network.
- **PAT** (preferential attachment) uses the mean degree of the already-known words it connects to.

This is the likelihood the old webppl models optimized; here α is fit by maximum likelihood.
The predictors are z-scored over the pooled TD + ASD growth data, so α is on the same scale for both groups.
Months run from the earliest to the latest rounded AoA in each group.

```{r growth}
growth <- aoa %>% group_by(group) %>%
  group_modify(function(x, key) {
    am <- setNames(round(x$aoa), x$definition)
    make_growth(am, nets, sort(unique(am)))
  }) %>% ungroup()

growth_preds <- c("sem_PAC", "sem_PAT", "phono_PAC", "phono_PAT")
growth <- growth %>% mutate(across(all_of(growth_preds), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))

models <- c(map(growth_preds, ~ .x) %>% setNames(growth_preds),
            list(combined = growth_preds))
growth_fits <- growth %>% group_by(group) %>%
  group_modify(function(g, key)
    imap_dfr(models, ~ fit_growth(g, .x) %>% mutate(model = .y))) %>%
  ungroup()

growth_fits %>% filter(model != "combined") %>%
  select(group, predictor, estimate, lower, upper, mcfadden_r2) %>%
  arrange(predictor, group) %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "Single-predictor growth models")
```

```{r growth-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
growth_fits %>%
  mutate(model = ifelse(model == "combined", "Combined", "Individual")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = predictor, color = group, shape = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), position = position_dodge(width = .6)) +
  labs(x = "α (log-odds of being learned next, per SD)", y = NULL)
```

Group differences in α (Wald z, ASD − TD):

```{r growth-diff}
growth_fits %>%
  select(group, model, predictor, estimate, se) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(estimate, se)) %>%
  mutate(diff = estimate_ASD - estimate_TD,
         z = diff / sqrt(se_ASD^2 + se_TD^2),
         p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))) %>%
  select(model, predictor, estimate_TD, estimate_ASD, diff, z, p) %>%
  kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r save}
save(aoa, words, static_coefs, growth_fits,
     file = sprintf("data/nda_private/network_results%s%s%s.Rds",
                    if (params$exclude_dx_unconfirmed) "_dxconfirmed" else "",
                    if (params$tier_A_only) "_tierA" else "",
                    if (params$include_flagged) "_withflagged" else ""))
```
